headline: Panel-level reference frameworks reconcile plant genome diversity across assemblies
label: Plant Genomic Reference Resources
summary: Multi-accession wheat and cereal panels now demand consistent annotation of repeats, genes, and sequence diversity across assemblies.
synthesis: The dominant thread is a shift from single-genome references toward panel-level representations that are reconciled or annotated consistently across assemblies. WheatPanRef yields an 18.87-Gb linear pan-reference for wheat from reconciled Chinese Spring assemblies plus non-CS sequences from 37 accessions. Earl Grey ParTEA builds a shared non-redundant transposable element library across genome panels for consistent comparative TE annotation, while TideCluster clusters tandem repeat arrays into family catalogs with consensus monomers without requiring a reference. The cereal pangene atlas reports pangene membership rising 59-264% across roughly 500 gene families in four cereals relative to single-genome analyses. Genomes2Genes extends the comparative theme by converting Progressive Cactus alignments into validated coding sequence alignments for extant and ancestral species. What is new is explicit reconciliation of diversity across panels rather than per-genome annotation. A separate maize and Brassica rapa study, which links recombination rate and chromatin context to subgenome identity, is related only through its use of genomic and epigenomic features.
